stories.headline: NASA Unveils $20B Moon Base Plan, Cancels Lunar Gateway Space Station

key_facts.fact: NASA canceled the Lunar Gateway orbital station and will redirect its components toward a $20 billion base on the moon's surface over seven years.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA announced on Tuesday it has canceled plans to deploy a space station in lunar orbit and will instead use components from the project to build a $20 billion base on the moon's surface.

key_facts.fact: The base will be built in three phases: Phase 1 (2026-28) focuses on robotic missions and scouting south pole sites, Phase 2 (2029-31) begins construction with two crewed missions per year, Phase 3 (2032+) enables sustained human presence.
key_facts.excerpt: Phase 1, running from 2026 to 2028, 'is all about getting to the moon reliably.' Phase 2, from 2029 through 2031, starts building the base... Phase 3, beginning 2032, will enable 'long distance and long duration human exploration' on the moon.

key_facts.fact: NASA plans to launch a nuclear-powered spacecraft called Space Reactor 1 Freedom to Mars before end of 2028, demonstrating advanced nuclear electric propulsion in deep space.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA also disclosed plans to launch a spacecraft called Space Reactor 1 Freedom to Mars before the end of 2028 in a mission it said would demonstrate advanced nuclear electric propulsion in deep space.

key_facts.fact: NASA foresees spending $10 billion each on Phases 1 and 2, with Phase 3 costing an additional $10 billion or more through at least 2036.
key_facts.excerpt: Garcia-Galan said NASA foresees spending $10 billion each on Phases 1 and 2. Phase 3, lasting to at least 2036, would cost an additional $10 billion or more.

key_facts.fact: Administrator Jared Isaacman made the announcement at the 'Ignition' event at NASA headquarters on March 24, as the U.S. races to return to the moon before China sends astronauts there around 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Isaacman, who was sworn in at the agency in December, made the announcement at the opening of a day-long event at NASA's Washington headquarters at which he outlined a raft of changes he is making to the agency's flagship moon program Artemis.

key_facts.fact: The plan includes deploying a fleet of drones and laying groundwork for using nuclear power on the lunar surface in the next few years.
key_facts.excerpt: The plans for the moon base included an aim to send more robotic landers, deploy a fleet of drones and lay the groundwork for using nuclear power on the lunar surface in the next few years.

stories.headline: Isar Aerospace Spectrum Second Flight Scrubbed by Automated Abort at T-0

key_facts.fact: The automated launch abort system activated at T-0 on March 25, preventing engine ignition after the range was initially not ready to support the launch, extending the countdown.
key_facts.excerpt: Launch Status: Scrubbed - First the range was not ready to support the launch which guided to an extended countdown, then there was no engine ignition at T-Zero because the automated launch abort system came into effect.

key_facts.fact: The 'Onward and Upward' mission was Spectrum's qualification flight carrying six ESA-backed payloads from universities and companies including TU Berlin, University of Maribor, EnduroSat, NTNU, TU Wien, and Dcubed.
key_facts.excerpt: This flight is designated a qualification flight, after last year's first test flight. The Spectrum rocket will host six payloads.

key_facts.fact: Spectrum is a two-stage launch vehicle standing 28 meters tall with ten engines, targeting payloads up to 1,000 kg to low Earth orbit, at an estimated price of EUR 10 million per launch.
key_facts.excerpt: Rocket Height: 28 m. Payload to Orbit: LEO 1,000 kg. Lift-Off Thrust: 675 Kilonewtons. Fairing: 2 m diameter. Stages: 2.

key_facts.fact: Isar Aerospace is backed by ESA's 'Boost!' programme, which supports European commercial launch vehicle development.
key_facts.excerpt: Isar Aerospace is backed by the European Space Agency (ESA) 'Boost!' programme.

key_facts.fact: The first Spectrum test flight in March 2025 flew for 30 seconds, clearing the launch pad and proving the rocket could achieve liftoff.
key_facts.excerpt: This launch comes after the rocket's first test flight, that flew for 30 seconds, clearing the launch pad and proved Spectrum can achieve one of the hardest parts of space transportation: liftoff.

stories.headline: Rocket Lab Scrubs ESA Celeste LEO Navigation Satellite Launch Due to Weather

key_facts.fact: Weather conditions over Launch Complex 1 in Mahia, New Zealand violated cloud and lightning commit criteria, forcing Rocket Lab to stand down from the Celeste mission on March 25.
key_facts.excerpt: Rocket Lab launch of Europe's 1st 2 'Celeste' navigation satellites scrubbed due to weather.

key_facts.fact: A weather system passing through the region means the next target launch date will be set once it clears, likely a delay of several days.
key_facts.excerpt: A weather system is passing through the region in the coming days, so our next target launch date will be set once that passes.

key_facts.fact: The 'Daughter of the Stars' mission would deploy two IOD satellites to 510 km LEO orbit as part of ESA's Celeste program to test LEO Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (LEO-PNT) technology complementing the Galileo system.
key_facts.excerpt: Rocket Lab will launch a dedicated Electron mission for the European Space Agency (ESA) for the first time, to deploy the first pair of satellites for a future European navigation mission in low Earth orbit named 'Celeste'.

key_facts.fact: The Celeste constellation will eventually comprise 11 satellites testing innovative signals across multiple frequencies to boost European navigation resilience and performance.
key_facts.excerpt: This is just the beginning: 11 satellites, innovative signals across multiple frequencies, a step towards more robust positioning and timing for Europe.

key_facts.fact: The two IOD spacecraft were built by Thales Alenia Space and GMV, Europe's satellite navigation prime contractors.
key_facts.excerpt: Rocket Lab will launch two 'Celeste' IOD spacecraft for ESA, provided by European satellite prime contractors Thales Alenia Space and GMV.

stories.headline: SpaceX Launches 54 Starlink Satellites in Two Back-to-Back Missions Within 9 Hours

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched 25 Starlink V2 Mini satellites from Vandenberg SFB on a Falcon 9 (Starlink Group 17-17) at approximately 02:39 UTC on March 26, after rescheduling from the previous day.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Space Force will support the launch of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket Wednesday between 4:03 and 8:03 p.m., sending 25 Starlink satellites to low-Earth orbit from Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg.

key_facts.fact: A second Falcon 9 launched 29 Starlink v2 Mini satellites from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at 11:22 UTC on March 26, roughly 9 hours after the Vandenberg mission.
key_facts.excerpt: As the Falcon 9 rocket soared into the sky, carrying 29 Starlink satellites, it marked a significant milestone in SpaceX's journey.

key_facts.fact: The Cape Canaveral booster was flying for its 27th time, one of SpaceX's most-flown boosters, having previously launched NASA Crew-6, SES, and USSF missions.
key_facts.excerpt: The Falcon 9 first-stage booster's impressive flight record. With 27 previous missions under its belt, including notable launches for NASA, SES, and the US Space Force.

key_facts.fact: The Cape Canaveral launch was SpaceX's 37th orbital mission of 2026 and the 21st from Florida's Space Coast this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Marking the 21st orbital rocket launch of the year from Florida's Space Coast.

key_facts.excerpt: SuperView Neo 2-05 & 06. Launch Success. Liftoff Time (GMT) 22:51:00 Wednesday March 25, 2026.

key_facts.fact: The satellites were built by CAST for China Siwei Survey and Mapping Technology Co. Ltd. and deployed to sun-synchronous orbit from Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center.

stories.headline: Lucid Bots Raises $20M Series B to Scale Autonomous Cleaning Drone Platform

key_facts.fact: Lucid Bots raised an oversubscribed $20 million Series B co-led by Cubit Capital and Idea Fund Partners, bringing total funding to $34 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Lucid Bots, the leading platform for autonomous exterior cleaning in the United States, today announced it has raised an oversubscribed $20 million Series B round co-led by Cubit Capital and Idea Fund Partners.

key_facts.fact: The company's operator network has surpassed $75 million in jobs completed with nearly 1,000 robots deployed nationwide, growing from 100 to 700 units in less than five months.
key_facts.excerpt: The drone provider said it has experienced rapid growth, increasing deployments from 100 to nearly 700 units in less than five months.

key_facts.fact: Lucid Bots launched a power tether option for its Sherpa cleaning drone enabling unlimited flight time, garnering nearly $1 million in pre-orders.
key_facts.excerpt: Its Sherpa drone now supports the spraying of sealing/coating additives as well as paint. To support the new applications, the system can now be equipped with a power tether for unlimited flight time... garnered nearly $1 million in pre-orders.

key_facts.fact: The company launched Lucid Refresh, a Robotics-as-a-Service subscription platform letting operators access drones, the Lavo AI pressure washing robot, fleet software, training, and support without upfront capital.
key_facts.excerpt: Lucid Bots' new Lucid Refresh platform offers a subscription-based approach to robotic cleaning. It allows operators to access drones, ground robots, software, and support without upfront capital investment.

key_facts.fact: Funding will scale commercial operations, expand domestic manufacturing in Charlotte, NC, and accelerate product rollout including the new Lavo AI autonomous ground-based pressure washing robot.
key_facts.excerpt: The raise brings total funding to $34 million and will be used to scale the company's commercial operations, expand its domestic manufacturing capacity in Charlotte, and accelerate the rollout of its RaaS offering Lucid Refresh.

stories.headline: Ukrainian OSIRIS AI Unveils Combat-Tested UEB-1 AI Interceptor Drone at 315 km/h

key_facts.fact: OSIRIS AI presented the UEB-1 interceptor drone at the Xpotential 2026 exhibition in Dusseldorf, Germany, designed to intercept high-speed aerial targets at up to 315 km/h.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian developer OSIRIS AI unveiled its new UEB-1 interceptor drone, capable of reaching speeds of up to 315 km/h, at the Xpotential exhibition in Dusseldorf.

key_facts.fact: The drone uses the OSIRIS DroneOS platform with AI for autonomous trajectory prediction and object tracking, requiring minimal operator involvement.
key_facts.excerpt: The system uses artificial intelligence to predict where a target is going and to track it effectively.

key_facts.fact: Specs include 18 km flight range, 10+ minutes endurance, 3.1 kg total weight with 0.5 kg payload, and a carbon fiber frame measuring 370 x 370 x 550 mm.
key_facts.excerpt: The UEB-1's technical specifications include a flight range of up to 18 kilometers and an endurance of over 10 minutes. With a total weight of 3.1 kg, the drone carries a 0.5 kg payload.

key_facts.fact: The drone has been tested in combat conditions and is part of the OSIRIS AI ecosystem for countering aerial threats from the Russian Federation.
key_facts.excerpt: The flight range is up to 18 km, and the drone itself has already been tested in combat conditions. OSIRIS UEB-1 is reportedly part of the OSIRIS AI ecosystem for countering aerial threats.

key_facts.fact: OSIRIS AI has production facilities in Ukraine and Poland with an R&D center in Krakow, funded by foreign investment received in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: OSIRIS AI's production facilities are located in Ukraine and Poland, and a research and development (R&D) center is located in Krakow.
